records.statement: In an experiment the investigator assigns the explanatory condition; random assignment is a defining design feature used to balance treatment groups and support causal comparison, unlike an observational study in which exposure is observed rather than assigned.

For randomized clinical trials, preserving the initial randomization in analysis is important for preventing bias, and the full analysis set should stay as close as possible to the intention-to-treat principle.

Interrupted time-series analysis uses outcomes measured over time before and after an intervention; simple pre/post comparison can be misleading because pre-interruption trend and autocorrelation must be considered.
records.section: What is ITS Analysis? / Time Series Caveats

records.statement: Interrupted time-series analysis can estimate an immediate level change, a sustained slope change, or both following an intervention.
Probability sampling gives population units known selection chances; simple random, stratified and cluster sampling are probability-based designs, while convenience sampling is non-probability based.

UN household-survey guidance treats simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster and multistage sampling as distinct probability-sampling strategies and emphasizes probability sampling at each stage of selection.

A census/complete enumeration differs from a sample survey because data are collected for the target population rather than selected sample units; surveys are often used when complete enumeration is impractical because of time or cost.
